[[File:Kasugasui.jpeg|thumb|250px|right|Kasuga Spring (春日水)]]
'''Kasuga Shrine''' (春日神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Myozan, Tokushima City|ja|眉山町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myozan, Tokushima City|qq=}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is situated on the eastern foothills of {{ill|Mount Bizan|ja|眉山|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan|qq=}}.
== History ==
The shrine traces its origins to a {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga-taisha|lt=Kasuga Shrine|ja|春日祠|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga Shrineja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} enshrined at the Kasuga territory in {{ill|Tomi-da|ja|富田庄|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tomi-daja_comment=jawiki redirects to 富田荘}} (modern {{ill|Irida|ja|入田町|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Irida|qq=}}, Tokushima City), a former estate of Kasuga Shrine in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|qid=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}. It is said to have been relocated to its current site at Otakiyama during the transfer of power to the {{ill|Hachisuka clan|en|Hachisuka clan|qid=Q2975261|lt=Hachisuka clan|1=Hachisuka clan}} in 1586, coinciding with the construction of {{ill|Tokushima Castle|en|Tokushima Castle|qid=Q8011246|lt=Tokushima Castle|1=Tokushima Castle}}. Another account suggests the shrine was moved from {{ill|Tamiya Village|ja|田宮村|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamiya Village|qq=}} along with Shofuku-ji Temple, which later became the shrine’s {{ill|Bettōji|ja|別当寺|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Bettōjicomment=enwiki is a redirect}} before its abolition in the early {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}.<ref>According to the ''Awa-shi'' (阿波志), compiled in 1815.</ref>
During the {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keicho era|1=Keichō}} (late 16th to early 17th century), the shrine was referred to as "Kasuga Daimyōjin" and received significant patronage from the Hachisuka clan, including an annual offering of 10 koku of rice. In 1873, it was officially renamed Kasuga Shrine and designated as a {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq=Gō-sha|qq=}}. The shrine also features "Kasuga Spring" (春日水), one of the notable {{ill|Mount Bizan springs|ja|眉山湧水群|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Bizan springs|qq=}}.

The shrine complex includes the following sub-shrines:

** Enshrines the deity formerly worshipped at Ryuo Shrine within Tokushima Castle.
* '''Wakamiya Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Ame-no-Kumunushi|ja|天忍雲根命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Kumunushija_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q91088537}})
* '''Akiba Shrine''' (deity: {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大御神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasuja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q455602}}, {{ill|Onamuchi|ja|大巳貴命|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Onamuchiqid=Q276944}}, {{ill|Haniyasubime|ja|埴安姫神|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haniyasubimeja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi|1=Ukemochi}}, {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|少彦名命|1=Sukunabikona|qq=draft|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikonaqid=Q3275687}})
